title: Your launch week, day by day
summary: Exactly what to post, send and check each day from launch day through day 7, so the week doesn't slip past you.

body.p: Launch week goes fast. Having each day written down before it starts means you spend it talking to readers instead of wondering what to do next. Set your launch date in the Author Studio launch planner and these tasks fill in with real dates.

list: Open your book page and check the title, price, description and both covers.
Buy nothing yet. Just make sure the Buy button works.
Write your launch email and launch post now, so tomorrow is easy.
Send your launch email in the morning.
Post on every place you're active, with the cover and one line from the book.
Send personal messages to your door-openers with the link.
Thank every single person who shares it, by name.

body.h: Day 2: The story behind the book

body.p: Post why you wrote it. A real moment works better than a summary: the night you started, the rejection you got, the person you wrote it for.
Share an early reader's honest reaction (with their OK), or a photo someone sent of the book in their hands.

body.h: Day 4: A taste of the inside

body.p: Share a short excerpt, a favorite page, or a tip from the book. Give something useful for free.
Email the early readers: "If you've finished, an honest review would mean a lot." One reminder is enough.

body.h: Day 6: Go live or show up somewhere

body.p: Do a short live video, a reading, a podcast chat or a local event. People buy from people.
Write down what you sold, what got the most attention and what you'd do again. Add the sales to your book's business tracker in the Author Studio so you can see the trend over months.

body.tip: A slow first week is normal for a first book. Most books sell over months and years, not days. Keep showing up.
